title: Feature branches
summary: Exercise 2: branch off develop, name it right, commit twice.

say.never: A **branch** is your own line of work that doesn't disturb anyone else's. `main` always holds the finished, tested robot code. `develop` collects finished features. Each new feature gets its own branch, and when it's done it joins `develop`.
say.bit: A branch is your own line of work. `main` stays production-ready, `develop` collects finished features, and each feature gets its own branch.

board.code:
main      o----------------------o   (only finished, tested work)
develop   o-------o--------o-----o   (features merge in here)
issue-12       \--o--o--/          (your work, off develop)

say.never: Start from `develop`, then create your branch and move onto it in one command. `-b` means "make a new branch". Name it after what you're working on, like `issue-12-turbo-boost`.
say.bit: Start from `develop`, then create and switch to your branch in one command.

board.code:
git checkout develop
git checkout -b issue-12-turbo-boost

marks.label: create the branch, then switch to it

say.never: Open the **terminal**: the typing area at the bottom of the screen where you give the computer instructions. Hold **Ctrl** and tap the backtick key, the one above **Tab**. Most of these exercises are easier there.
say.bit: These exercises are easiest in the terminal.

hint.never: press Ctrl and the backtick key (above Tab).

say.never: Type `cd 02-feature-branch` and press **Enter** to move into the folder. Then run the two commands from the board, one at a time, pressing **Enter** after each. Choose your own name that starts with `issue-12-`.
say.bit: `cd 02-feature-branch`, then run the two commands above.

hint.never: create a branch starting with issue-12- off develop.

say.never: Look at the bottom-left corner. It shows which branch you're on right now. It's the fastest way to check before you save work, so you don't commit to the wrong branch.
say.bit: The bottom-left corner shows the branch the editor is looking at. It's the quickest check before you commit.

say.never: This exercise wants **two separate** commits. Small commits with clear messages tell the story of your work, one step at a time, like chapters in a book. Make a change, add and commit it. Then make another change and do it again.
say.bit: The exercise wants **two separate** commits: small commits, each with a clear message, tell the story of the work.

board.code:
git add FEATURES.md
git commit -m "Describe the turbo boost button"
# edit again...
git add FEATURES.md
git commit -m "Add the turbo boost speed limit"

say.never: Type `git log --oneline` and press **Enter**. You should see your two commits on top of the starting one, newest first.
say.bit: Run `git log --oneline` to see your two commits on top of the starting one.
